title: Creating 3D Garment
content: **Objective** Create Garment content using CLO and Marvelous Designer software. **Required & Recommended** When creating and uploading a Garment file, please follow the rules below. **[Required]** * The garment file format must be *zprj, *zpac. * The garment should be simulated on your avatar (including hangers). * The garment file may include an official CLO/Marvelous Designer avatar or an avatar with an authorized resale license when you upload an item in the Garment Category. * The sewing lines should not be twisted. * Collision issues between layers should be resolved if you are designing a layered garment. * It is not possible to delete/add/replace the Trim and Fabric files after Publish. * It is not possible to add, delete, or replace different Design Sources after Publish, for garments that include Design Sources. * The majority of the components should consist of 2D patterns produced by pattern-making in CLO or Marvelous Designer software. * The 2D pattern should have a reasonable particle distance. The recommended particle distance value is 5 to 20. * 2D patterns should be arranged as neatly as possible in the center. Avoid overlapping patterns in the 2D Pattern window. * 2D patterns that are the same pieces(e.g. Jackets, Pants, etc.) should be close to each other and should be easily recognized as one piece. * The unnecessary notches and baselines inside the 2D pattern should be deleted before publishing. **[Recommended]** * The garment should have Fitting Suit information for compatibility with the Auto Fitting function. * The garment should be saved after deactivating the Strengthen, Freeze feature. * You have to save the garment after simulating it in the A pose or the T pose. * A collision between trims should be resolved if trim category items (e.g., Buttons, Zippers, Hardware, Fasteners, Notions) are added to the garment. **Details** **1\. Loading Avatar** \- Use the default avatar from the software. Library ▶ Avatar \- Use a customized Avatar from the software. Main Menu ▶File ▶ Open ▶ Avatar **※Fitting Suit** \- CLO Software Users CLO's default avatar is wearing a Fitting Suit. Fitting Suit is a device that helps the CLO's Auto Grading function to work. If both avatars have Fitting Suit information when wearing the same 3D costume to different size avatars, they can be draped to the appropriate size for each avatar without any special pattern modification. If the outfit uploaded by the Seller is a ZPAC file using the CLO default avatar, the Auto Grading feature makes it easier for buyers to use 3D costumes. \- Marvelous Designer Software Users The Marvelous Designer default avatar is also wearing a Fitting Suit. You can also add Fitting Suit information to your avatar if you are using the Marvelous Designer software version 10 or higher. Please refer to the [link](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2NjCNZxcYtk&t=77s) for detailed instructions. **2\. Creating Patterns / Sewing / Simulation** * Create patterns using the pattern generation tool from the 2D window. * Sew patterns created by using the sewing tool from the 3D or 2D window. * When sewing is completed, press the simulation button to simulate the costume on the avatar. **※Particle distance** For smooth operation speed, we recommend working at the default value of 20. When submitting the final costume file, make sure that the particle spacing is set as a reasonable value. By default, 5 is recommended, and 3 is recommended if the pattern is small. **※Layer** When creating a costume with multiple layers, it must collide between layers. You can set the order of layers by setting the layer value from the simulation properties pane. It is recommended to change the value to zero after the simulation is complete. ![Property_Editor.jpeg](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775564555673) **3\. Setting up textures** From the Properties Editor, you can add/modify textures that are used for garments. ![Property_Editor_2.jpeg](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775531859865) **4\. Saving Files** Save the garment file according to the specified file format. \- ZPAC Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Save as ▶ Garment If you save it through the above path, the only garment except the avatar is automatically saved. In this case, the file extension is saved as ZPAC. \- ZPRJ Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Save as ▶ Project If you save it through the above path, the garment including the avatar is saved. In this case, the file extension is saved as .zprj. ※Note: Only ZPAC or ZPRJ files can be uploaded in the Garment category. **5\. Creating Render Image** Allows all 3D Window screenshots or images rendered by other software. **6\. CONNECT UPLOAD - Entering Asset Description** **When uploading the GARMENT to CONNECT, please provide detailed information about the asset for the convenience of customers.** **If detailed information is missing, asset registration may be rejected during the item approval process.** ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775532040729) **1\. UPLOAD (Mandatory) ** Confirm the uploaded asset name and format and replace the file by pressing the **REUPLOAD** button if necessary. **2\. TITLE (**Mandatory**)** Please enter the asset name that will be displayed on CONNECT. By default, the uploaded asset's name will be set automatically as the DEFAULT TITLE. **3\. DESCRIPTION ** If you are selling a physical product, please provide the sales page URL in the description. When you enter the URL with 'http://' or 'https://,' the link will be generated automatically. **4\. TAGS** **'TAGS'** is a target keyword that helps customers search and amplify your content's reach. Entering the type of assets for sale will help customers when searching for the items. **5\. ATTACHMENT** You can attach files relating to the Garment. However, it is impossible to track attachment files attached to **'ATTACHMENT'** are being used. **6\. ADD SUB-IMAGES** You can additionally add images that highlight the characteristics of the Garment. If you are selling a physical product, it is also acceptable to upload actual photos. **7\. THUMBNAIL** Register an image that well showcases the characteristics of the Garment. If you applied a material that is visible only in the render, please register the rendered image. Registering the images where items are not visible or images unrelated to the item may lead to rejection during the item approval process.

title: Create Clothing
content:
Design the clothing that suits the game. Check the availability of the clothing before you start the design. * **Available Clothing Types** * Top + Bottom * Top + Bottom + Outerwear ```
⚠️ You do not create the following items: Hats, Socks (including ‘Leg warmer’), Shoes.
``` * * * ### ### **1\. Create Clothing** 1. Import the desired avatar (.avte) 2. Create the clothing to fit the avatar. * All trims on the garment should be attached using the Glue function. ```
💡Check the following guidelines when creating clothing
``` * To maximize the use of polygons, it’s recommended to delete the hidden parts of the clothing, especially when clothing has multiple layers and heavy linings. *Example) Pocket linings, the parts of the clothing obscured by layering, etc * ![Delete mesh_ref.png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51505335332505) * ![Delete mesh_ref2.png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51505351024281) * ![Delete mesh_ref3.png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51505351026585) * When creating skirts, make them within the guidelines indicated on the avatar for fitting stability. * ![이미지 022.jpg](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51505351028377) * The length of the sleeve should not intrude below the guideline indicated on the avatar’s hand. * ![이미지 020.jpg](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51505351032089) * When creating the pants, the length of the pants should not touch the ground. * Must use the provided template shoes ONLY for the CONNECT. ### ### **2\. Garment Simulation** Apply all the garments to the template avatar and simulate them for stabilization. If the value ‘**Add’l Thickness - Collision (mm)** ’ is lower than the default value of **2.5mm** , the collision between garments during simulation may become unstable. Therefore, it is strongly recommended to set the value of ‘**Add’l Thickness - Collision (mm)** ’ to **2.5mm** or higher before the simulation. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51505537924889) ### ### **3\. Modifying all patterns to Quad-Type** 1. Select all patterns (Ctrl+A). 2. Change the mesh type (Mesh Style) in the Property Editor to **Quad(Optimized**). ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51505553523865)
```
⚠️ Please avoid using the ‘Quad (Grid)’ option in the Mesh Type (Mesh Style).
``` ### **4\. Modifying Top Stitch Type** Please change the type of the top stitches used in the garment to ‘**Texture type**.’ 1. Click the ‘**Topstitch** ’ tab in the Object Browser. 2. Select all Stitches. 3. Change the stitch type to ‘**Texture** ’ in the Property Editor. ```
⚠️ Please note that the Custom TopStitch currently provided by CONNECT does not support Texture type, so it cannot be used in EveryWear.
``` ### ### ### **5\. Modifying the thickness properties of the garment** The thickness type of the garment affects the polygon counts, so it should be defined before beginning the optimization process. If you are creating the thick type of garment, please change the ‘Garment Rendering Style’ mode to ‘**Thick Textured Surface (Alt+1)**.’ ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51505875616537) **Setting Thickness Properties** The pattern thickness property can be set in the Geometry option of the pattern’s Property Editor. For more details on **Geometry properties** , please check the [Documentation](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358238232985-Add-Pattern-Thickness). **How to Set Thickness Property** 1. Select the pattern for which you want to adjust the thickness property. 2. After selecting the pattern, go to **Property → Geometry → Add’l Thickness - Rendering (mm)** and change the value to **3**. It’s recommended to use a value of **1–3** to make the garment thickness appear slightly exaggerated compared to real clothing. You may adjust this to be thinner or thicker depending on the material or specific case. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51505875619097) 3. Select the **Extrusion Direction** and whether to generate each side of the pattern. If the **Extrusion Direction** is set to “Forward” or “Both,” the thickness will be added outward, which can make the garment’s silhouette appear larger. Therefore, **please set all patterns to “Backward” by default** when working. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51505842884249)
``` 💡 In some cases, it may be necessary to keep the visible outer surface while deleting the invisible inner surface to optimize it. In this case, you can optimize by maintaining the Front Face option checked (status: On) and unchecking (status: Off) the Back Face option. How to use : 1. Select all patterns (Ctrl+A).
2. Property Editor → Check off the Back Face option in the Geometry section.
3. Select the patterns for which you can see the inner surface.
4. Check the Back Face option (status: On).
``` 4\. Set the side surface properties of the pattern using the Side Geometry option. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51508838744985) The Curvature (%) and Resolution settings under Side Geometry control the curvature and segmentation of the pattern’s side surfaces. A higher Resolution value results in more detailed segmentation, while a lower value maintains a flatter shape. (Setting the value to 0 disables the side surface entirely.) Since this setting directly affects optimization, we recommend setting the Resolution to 2 or higher only when segmentation is necessary for the pattern’s side.
``` 💡 Comparison of Side Geometry Based on Curvature (%) and Resolution Values
``` ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51508819940249) ### **6\. Applying Fabric Materials** Apply appropriate fabric materials that match the garment design. You can either use fabric presets (`*.zfab`) available in the CLO/MD Library or select suitable materials from the [**CONNECT**](https://connect.clo-set.com/). Proper fabric application will affect texture baking results and help achieve a more realistic surface appearance. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51509243441561) ### **7\. Modifying Garments** Adjust the patterns to make sure that the garments dressed by the template avatar work smoothly in EveryWear. Please refer to the ['**Tips &Tricks**'](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/en-us/articles/51485404185497-Tips-Ticks) and adjust the garments according to the relevant case.

title: What are the W-8BEN, W-8BEN-E, and W-9 forms that need to be completed in Seller Info?
content: If a buyer on CONNECT resides in the United States, withholding tax must be paid in the U.S. The tax rate is applied based on the treaty agreement between the U.S. and the seller's country. This tax is automatically calculated by CONNECT when the buyer purchases the item. The W-8BEN, W-8BEN-E, and W-9 forms are U.S. tax forms used to provide important information from the Connect platform for tax reporting purposes. Here's what they mean: **W-8BEN** Used by individuals who are non-U.S. residents to certify their foreign status and claim any applicable tax treaty benefits for reduced or exempt U.S. withholding taxes. Typical for individuals who sell items on Connect and are not U.S. citizens or residents. **W-8BEN-E** Business entities outside the U.S. use it to certify their foreign status and claim treaty benefits. Applicable to non-U.S. companies or organizations selling on Connect. **W-9** Used by U.S. persons (individuals or entities) to provide their Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) to the payer for tax reporting. Required for U.S.-based sellers on the platform. Filling out these forms correctly ensures compliance with tax regulations. If you need help determining which form to complete, consult a tax professional.

content: **1) UV Packing** **Objective** Customize the ‘resolution’ and ‘spacing’ of UV and automatically reposition the UV shell accordingly. **Details** ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51925725416729) 1. Go to the ‘UV packing settings’ window. * The EveryWear window will close for a moment. **1-1) UV Packing_Option** **Objective** Set and apply UV Packing-related options. **Details** ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775749149849) 1. Option to set the UV accuracy from 1 to 5. Values closer to 5 will pack the UVs more accurately to their original form but may increase the amount of calculation and packing time. 2. Rotation : When enabled, it allows for the rotation of the UV shell. 4. Advanced Placement : When enabled, it uses an advanced calculation method to achieve optimal placement with minimal empty space, but the process may take longer as the number of patterns increases. 5. Fill the U:0, V:0 tiles with the selected UV Shell. 6. Pack the selected UV Shell directly by specifying the target tile. 7. Initialize all user-specified option values. 8. Pack UVs according to the specified option values. 9. (Normal & A.O.) **Details** ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51925725421337) 1. Create a Normal Map and Ambient Occlusion (A.O) Map. 2. Adjust the intensity of the Baked Normal Map. 3. The number of rays of light sampled per pixel. * Increase this value for higher-quality, but please keep in mind that it will also increase calculation time. 4. Activate this option to preview the baked map in the 3D viewport. This allows you to see the changes in real-time. 5. Delete Baked Map **3) Material List** **Objective** Copy an existing material or create a new material, and apply it to the selected pattern as desired. **Details** ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51925725422873) 1. Add a new Material item. 2. Copy a Material. 3. Assign the selected Material to the selected Object. 4. Delete the selected Material. * You cannot delete the material that is already assigned to the Object.

title: Garment Tab
content: **1) Polygon Optimization** **Objective** In the Garment Tab, adjust the Poly Count of the garment to match the platform you intend to export it to. **Details** ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51927187502873) 1. You can manually input the desired Poly Count. 2. It will display the current Polygon Count of the garment, including Trims. * When the pattern’s mesh style is changed to Quad, it displays the total number of polygons, including the number of polygons changed to Quad and the remaining Triangles. * You can also check the polygon counts in the bottom left corner of the 3D window. * ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775738060185) 3. It will display the current Polygon Count of the garment, including Trims, converted into Triangles. 4. It shows the Poly Count of the Avatar. 5. Optimize the garment mesh according to the input provided in #1. * If you enter a value smaller than the modifiable range, the value will be automatically adjusted and applied as the minimum value (variable). 6. It switches to the Mask Brush tool. The EveryWear window temporarily closes, and the Brush tool appears in the upper-right corner of the 3D window. 7. Move to the Auto Seal tool. The EveryWear window will briefly close, and the Auto Seal tool will appear in the upper-right corner of the 3D window. **1-1) Applying Mask Brush** **Objective** Use the Mask Brush in the 3D and 2D windows to define the Mask area. **Details** ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/49331558190873) 1. Switch tabs to set the surfaces where the Mask will be applied. * The Front and Back tab of the Mask Brush are based on the 2D pattern window, while in the 3D window, you can mask both sides. 2. Select a type to define how the area will be selected. (Brush / Box / Lasso) 3. You can select a mode to either add or subtract from the mask area. 4. Adjust the size of the Mask Brush. 5. When this option is enabled, all closed area that includes the selected point will be masked. ※ This option is only available when the Type is set to Brush. 6. When this option is enabled, you can work on both the front and back sides simultaneously. 7. Clear all applied masks. 8. Mode, Size, Select Enclosed Region and Double-Sided Brush settings will be reset. 9. The Mask Brush window will close, and the EveryWear window will open. **1-2) Auto Seal** **Objective** The Auto Seal feature is used to close the holes inside the garment, preventing the interior from being visible. * This feature helps close open areas of the garment, such as sleeves or hems, preventing the inner side from appearing empty. * By closing these holes, you can prevent the inner side of the garment from being exposed when the avatar moves, resulting in a more polished final look. * Enclosed or hidden mesh is automatically masked to optimize performance and prevent the use of unnecessary geometry. ** Details ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51927187504281) ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775689910169) ** 1. Click the Auto Seal button. 2. Create Guidelines. \- Disc Mode: Create a disc by placing three points on the pattern. The curve (or path) cut by this disc becomes the guideline. \- 3D Pen Mode: Draw a curve (or path) on the garment to create the guideline (similar to the previous 3P Pen). Align the last point with the first point to complete the curve (or path). 3. Select Hidden Areas. \- Select the direction in which the face should be created, then apply ‘Auto Seal.’ ※ Note : Auto Seal is only activated in 3D view when the Rendering Mode is set to Thick. **2) Rigging** **Objective** Rigging the garments to the avatar. * Rigging is a fundamental aspect of 3D process, creating a skeleton structure with joints and bones to enable animations for 3D models. * EveryWear's rigging merges the outfit with the avatar's joints, allowing them to move together. * This rigging process also involves weight painting, which determines how much each part of the outfit is influenced by the movement of the avatar’s joints. This rigging process involves setting up and creating the controllable structure for the movement of the avatar and the outfit. * CLO and Marvelous Designer specialize in detailed and realistic clothing animations through advanced garment simulations. However, for gaming purposes, the considerable data size of simulation-based clothing animations may not always be efficient. * Therefore, EveryWear optimizes by utilizing Rigging instead of simulations to effectively synchronize the movements of outfits and avatars, prioritizing efficiency. * Starting from version 2024.2 of CLO and Marvelous Designer, the accuracy of Auto-rigging has been further improved. **Details** ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51927187511321) 1. Clothing is automatically rigged to the avatar. * When rigging is applied, the ‘Update’ and ‘Brush tools’ will appear as shown in <Image2> * If the avatar does not have joints or if there are multiple avatars within the same project, rigging will not proceed. * When attempting to simulate the garment in the rigging state, the following warning message will be displayed. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775739338009) 1. * * Yes : The rigging information will be deleted as soon as the costume is simulated, and the rigging menu returns to its initial state. * No : The simulation will not proceed, and the existing rigging information will be maintained. * 1-1. All Patterns: Updates the rigging for all patterns, regardless of the current pattern selection. * 1-2. Selected Patterns: Updates the rigging only for the currently selected pattern(s). 2. Target Joint : Used to exclude or remove specific joint weights from the rigging target. \- If the rigging has already been applied: After setting the Target Joint, click Update to remove all weights applied to that joint. 3. Show Avatar Joints : Displays the avatar’s joint points in the 3D window. 4. Max Influence Joints : Set the maximum number of joints that can affect each vertex. 5. Switch to Bind Pose : Returns the avatar to its original pose defined during creation. \- It is independent of the loading pose or the most recent pose. \- If switched to Bind Pose when rigging is not applied, the current draping state may be altered. **\- Notes** \- It is recommended to perform rigging in the Bind Pose state. \- If rigging is performed in a non-Bind Pose state, artifacts may occur when editing weights. 6. All Patterns: Rigs/updates all patterns. 7. Selected Patterns: Rigs/updates only the selected patterns. * Tip: When rigging for the first time, use All Patterns to process all patterns. For partial edits, use the Selected Patterns option. * Tip: After checking Selected Patterns, click Update to re-rig only the selected patterns. 8. Re-rig based on the current state of the garment. 9. Navigate to the Brush tool. The EveryWear window momentarily closes, and the Brush tool appears in the upper right corner of the 3D window. **3) Brush_Weight** **Objective** Modify the weight value using the brush. * Weight Painting ensures the rigged outfit moves seamlessly with the avatar's motions. * Weight Painting adjusts joint influence on surrounding vertices for natural and fluid movements. * While EveryWear auto-distributes weights based on the avatar, it's essential to check for any outfit penetration or inaccuracies in motion. Make necessary weight adjustments if needed. **Details** ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51927157285273) 1. Set the Brush to Weight Mode. (Hotkey : Ctrl + ~) 2. Change the blend mode. (Hotkey : Ctrl + Tab) * Add : Add / Increase the weight value. * Subtract : Subtract / Decreases the weight value. * Smooth : Adjusts the weight value to match the surrounding areas. 3. Set Brush properties. * Strength : Adjust the intensity of the brush. (Hotkey : Alt + [ , ] ) * Size : Change the size of the brush. (Hotkey : [ , ] ) * Focal : Adjust the intensity difference between the center and edge of the brush. * Depth : Set the depth of the brush's influence. 4. Initialize the Brush property value. 5. Exit the Brush tool and go to the EveryWear window. **3-1) Applying Weight Brush** * After selecting the Avatar's Joint, users can adjust Weight value by using a brush to add or subtract. * Real-time Weight adjustments in 2D window are possible as well. * **Add Weight** * 1\. Select Brush Tool: Press the Brush icon to open the Brush tool. * 2\. Choose Brush Mode: Set the Brush to Weight Mode. * 3\. Select Blend Mode: Configure the Blend Mode to Add. * 4\. Adjust Brush Properties: Modify the size and strength of the Brush according to your desired operation. * 5\. Choose Joint: While holding down Ctrl, click on the Joint. The selected Joint will be highlighted in yellow. * 6\. Apply Add Weight: Click and drag over the area you want to apply the brush. As the Weight value increases, it will be represented with a deeper red color. * **Subtract Weight** * 1.Select Brush Tool: Press the Brush icon to open the Brush tool. * 2\. Choose Brush Mode: Set the Brush to Weight Mode. * 3\. Select Blend Mode: Configure the Blend Mode to Subtract. * 4\. Adjust Brush Properties: Modify the size and strength of the Brush according to your desired operation. * 5\. Choose Joint: While holding down Ctrl, click on the Joint. The selected Joint will be highlighted in yellow. * 6\. Apply Subtract Weight: Click and drag over the area you want to apply the brush. As the Weight value decreases, it will be represented with a deeper blue color. When the Weight value is 0, no weight color information will be displayed. * **Smooth (Single Joint)** * This function smooths the Joint weight of vertices based on the selected joint, softly adjusting the weight differences with surrounding vertices. * The sum of the joint weights for each vertex is always maintained at 1, and when the weight of the selected joint for a vertex is adjusted, the weights of the remaining joints are automatically scaled to maintain balance. However, if the weight of the selected joint is not different from that of surrounding vertices, no smoothing will occur. * 1\. Select Brush Tool: Press the Brush icon to open the Brush tool. * 2\. Choose Brush Mode: Set the Brush to Weight Mode. * 3\. Select Blend Mode: Configure the Blend Mode to Smooth (Single Joint). * 4\. Adjust Brush Properties: Modify the size and strength of the Brush according to your desired operation. * 5\. Choose Joint: While holding down Ctrl, click on the Joint. The selected Joint will be highlighted in yellow. * 6\. Apply Smooth Weight: Click and drag over the area you want to apply the brush. The Weight will be smoothly adjusted based on the surrounding values. * Tips By applying the 'Full Smooth' function to the selected joint's skin weight, you can evenly smooth across the entire selected joint with one click, eliminating the need for manually painting weight with the Smooth brush. * Usage: Click on the joint you want to modify to view its weight, then press Ctrl+Shift and click on the selected joint again. You can adjust the smoothing strength by modifying the 'strength' parameter under brush properties. * **Smooth (Multiple Joints)** * It operates for all joints, smoothing the joint weights of each vertex along with the weights of surrounding vertices. * This is similar to selecting and using all joints in the Single Brush. In this process, the joint weights of each vertex are adjusted smoothly and simultaneously, while the sum of the joint weights for each vertex always remains 1. * 1\. Select Brush Tool: Press the Brush icon to open the Brush tool. * 2\. Choose Brush Mode: Set the Brush to Weight Mode. * 3\. Select Blend Mode: Configure the Blend Mode to Smooth (Multiple Joints). * 4\. Adjust Brush Properties: Modify the size and strength of the Brush according to your desired operation. * 5\. Apply Smooth Weight: Click and drag over the area you want to apply the brush. The Weight will be smoothly adjusted based on the surrounding values. * **Joint Lock** * The Joint Lock feature is designed to influence only specific areas when modifying weights in situations such as the following: * When adjusting the weight value without affecting the selected joint. * When unrelated joints are causing the weight issues and need corrections (e.g., armpits, corners, sleeves, skirts, etc.). * When intricate weight adjustments are required for complex models. * Locked Joints will remain unaffected when adjusting other joints’ weight values. * 1\. Select Brush Tool: Press the Brush icon to open the Brush tool. * 2\. Choose Brush Mode: Set the Brush to Weight Mode. * 3\. Lock the Joint: Hold down Alt and click on the Joint. The Locked Joint will be highlighted in red. * To apply Lock to all joints, hold Alt and right-click on the desired joint. * 4\. Unlock the Joint: To unlock, Hold Alt and click on the locked Joint again. Once unlocked, the Joint will be displayed in white. * To unlock all joints, hold Alt and right-click on the desired joint. * **Hammering** * Hammering is a feature that automatically adjusts the weight values of a specific vertex to closely match the surrounding weight values when there is a significant disparity. * This feature comes in handy in situations where certain areas, like armpits, the bottom of pants, sleeves, and so on, are unintentionally affected by unwanted joints, resulting in awkward deformations or the strange spikes. * 1\. Select Brush Tool: Press the Brush icon to open the Brush tool. * 2\. Choose Brush Mode: Set the Brush to Weight Mode. * 3\. Select Joint: Hold down Ctrl and click on the joint. The selected joint will be highlighted in yellow. * 4\. Hammering: Hold down Shift and click on the desired vertex. When Shift is pressed, the mouse cursor changes from the brush shape to a red dot, indicating that it can recognize vertices. * **Copy Symmetric Weights** * This function allows you to copy the weight values from one side of a symmetric pattern to the opposite side. * By editing only one side and applying the same values to the other, you can reduce the time spent on weight adjustments. * 1\. Switch to Weight Brush mode. (Make sure no joints are selected.) * 2\. Select the pattern(s) whose weight values you want to copy. (Selection is possible in the 2D or 3D view.) * If multiple patterns are selected, the weight values of each pattern will be copied. * If both symmetric patterns are selected, the copy operation will not be performed. * 3\. Right Click → Copy Symmetric Weights to copy the weight values to the opposite symmetric pattern. * The joint-specific weight values applied to each pattern can be checked by selecting the corresponding joint. **4) Brush_Sculpt** **Objective** Use the Brush to modify the shape of the garment. **Details** ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51927157286297) 1. Set the Brush to Sculpt Mode. (Hotkey : Ctrl + ~) 2. Change the blend mode. (Hotkey : Ctrl + Tab) * Grab : Use this mode to grab and reshape the 3D clothing surface. * Smooth : Use this mode to make the 3D clothing surface smoother. * Fix Intersection : Use this mode to correct areas where intersections occur between the garment and the avatar or between the surfaces of the garment. 3. Set Brush properties. * Strength : Adjust the intensity of the brush. ( Hotkey : Ctrl + [ , ] ) * Size : Change the size of the brush. ( Hotkey : [ , ] ) * Focal : Adjust the difference between the brush center and edge intensity values. * Depth : Set the depth of the brush's influence. 4. Initialize the Brush property value. 5. Exit the Brush tool and go to the EveryWear window. **4-1) Applying ****Sculpt****Brush** * Using the Sculpt Brush allows users to modify the shape of the garment. * **Applying Grab Brush** * Utilize this brush when the garment penetrates inside the avatar or when garment layers overlap, causing visibility issues. * 1\. Select the Brush Tool: Open the Brush Tool by clicking on the Brush icon. * 2\. Choose Brush Mode: Set the Brush to Sculpt Mode. * 3\. Select Blend Mode: Set the Blend Mode to Grab. * 4\. Adjust Brush Properties: Modify the size and strength of the Brush according to your desired operation. * 5\. Apply Grab Brush: Click and drag over the area you want to apply the brush, and the selected area will move along with the mouse. Note that the Weight value will not have any effect. * **Applying Smooth Brush** * Utilize this brush to create a smoother surface for garments or to soften angular areas while modeling. * 1\. Select the Brush Tool: Open the Brush Tool by clicking on the Brush icon. * 2\. Choose Brush Mode: Set the Brush to Sculpt Mode. * 3\. Select Blend Mode: Set the Blend Mode to Smooth. * 4\. Adjust Brush Properties: Modify the size and strength of the Brush according to your desired operation. * 5\. Apply Smooth Brush: Click and drag over the area you want to apply the brush, and the surface will be smoothed based on its surroundings * **Applying Fix Intersection Brush** * Utilize this brush for areas where the garment intersects with the avatar or where garments overlap, as other existing brushes may struggle with these areas. * 1\. Select the Brush Tool: Open the Brush Tool by clicking on the Brush icon. * 2\. Choose Brush Mode: Set the Brush to Sculpt Mode. * 3\. Select Blend Mode: Set the Blend Mode to Fix Intersection. * 4\. Adjust Brush Properties: Modify the size and strength of the Brush according to your desired operation. * 5\. Apply Fix Intersection Brush : Apply the brush to the desired area to automatically correct intersections where the avatar or garments overlap.
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for optimizing polygon counts, applying rigging techniques, and utilizing sculpting brushes in garment design, ensuring a seamless integration between 3D clothing and avatars.

title: Building portfolio
content: ## **Objective** The portfolio is a page where you can introduce yourself and organize your items. ## **Details** **1\. Register CREATOR Information** ![portfolio_3.jpg](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/53247032566425) ① BANNER IMAGE | Register the image from the banner. The recommended size is 3200*280px. The file extensions that can be registered are png / jpg / jpeg / gif. The word limit is up to 250 characters. ## **2\. Upload Items** ### **2.1 Upload existing data transferred from CLOLLAB** * Transferred data from CLOLLAB is shown in Draft status, which is only visible to you. ![mceclip0.png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/53247049326745) * Clicking the item's image in Draft status will take you to the page to upload 3D files. * You can PUBLISH items only when uploading 3D files. * Currently, it is only possible to upload the items as Free or View Only. *In the case of Free and View Only Items, there is no separate inspection standard, and if you click PUBLISH, it will be posted on CONNECT immediately. * In the case of View Only, it is possible to change to Paid Items later. Please note that once you select Free, you cannot change to Paid Items in the future. * For more information on Free, View Only, and Paid Items, please click the [Pricing & License Options](https://clo-set-hc.zendesk.com/hc/ja-jp/articles/45303202752153) for reference. * For details on uploading, please click the [Uploading Item ](https://clo-set-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/360003330795)for reference. ### **2.2 Upload New Item** * Click the UPLOAD button at the bottom of the banner, and it will take you to the upload page. * For details on uploading, please click the [Uploading Item ](https://clo-set-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/360003330795)for reference. ## **3\. COLLECTION Tab** * The collection and subordinate items set by the creator are displayed. ※**What is COLLECTION?** COLLECTION is a unit for the compilation of items on a specific subject. ### **3.1 COLLECTION Settings** * You can edit it by clicking on the collection name. * You can add a collection by clicking the ADD NEW COLLECTION button. * You can delete the collection or edit its location by clicking the More button on the right. By default, one collection exists as a required value. ### **3.2 Items Administrations** * You can move the items by dragging them to the desired collection. * Depending on the item's status, the status is shown on the upper left of the thumbnail. ## **4\. ITEM Tab** All Items of the creator are displayed in the order of upload. You cannot change the order randomly. **5\. SHARE** Click the ![mceclip0.png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/53247032574105)SHARE button at the bottom of the banner. You can copy the link on the portfolio page.

title: Item Inspection
content: **Objective** Upload the item to CONNECT followed by the guidelines. * Free and View Only items are posted at the same time as you click the Publish button. * However, items that are already published may be rejected or blocked according to the guidelines. [※ Note: 3D File Status ](https://clo-set-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/45303163209881) * If the item is blocked, the item will be deleted by the operator. * If the item is rejected, you should modify the item according to the guidelines and publish it again. **Details** Please check the criteria of Reject and Block below and follow the guideline. 1. Block Criteria 2. Reject Criteria ## ## ※ **Block Criteria** If you do not follow the guidelines below, the item may be deleted by the operator. * Do not include content containing the Corporate Identity and Brand Identity of CLO or Marvelous Designer. * Do not contain content from unauthorized brands. * Do not copy products from specific brands. * Do not include content that does not have a redistribution license. * Do not include content purchased from similar sites. * Do not include words and content that adversely affect society. * Do not include content that promotes other marketplaces or digital stores or exposes social media accounts. * Do not include content that can cause other problems. ## ※ **Reject Criteria** Please upload the item by following the guidelines below. Items cannot be uploaded until they are modified. **1\. Common** All content in CONNECT must comply with the following criteria: * The title of the item must be appropriate to the uploaded file. * Tags, categories, and descriptions must be appropriate to the uploaded file. * The thumbnail and additional images be appropriate to the uploaded file. * The attached files should be appropriate to the uploaded file. * If the item is also selling the physical product, you must enter the URL of the sales page (e.g. [https://connect.clo-set.com/](https://connect.clo-set.com/)). * Each item can have only one file uploaded, and compressing multiple item files into a single archive and uploading it to the ATTACHMENT is not allowed. If multiple item files are uploaded to ATTACHMENT, they cannot be downloaded from the CONNECT library, and individual items will not be visible in the item page viewer. **2\. Item Guidelines** The detailed guidelines for each item type in CONNECT are as follows. [Garment] * The garment file format must be *zprj, *zpac. * The garment should be simulated on your avatar (including hangers). * The file should exclude avatars when you upload an item in Garment Category. * The sewing lines should not be twisted. * Collision issue between layers should be resolved, if you are designing a layered garment. * It is not possible to delete/add/replace the Trim and Fabric files after Publish. * It is not possible to delete/add/replace the original garment files after Publish, for garment using original garment files. * The majority of the components should consist of 2D patterns produced by pattern making in CLO or Marvelous Designer software. * The 2D pattern should have reasonable particle distance. The recommended particle distance value is 5 to 20. * 2D patterns should be arranged as neatly as possible in the center. Avoid overlapping patterns in the 2D Pattern window. * 2D patterns that are the same pieces(e.g. Jackets, Pants, etc.) should be close to each other and should be easily recognized as one piece. * The unnecessary notches and baselines inside the 2D pattern should be deleted before Publish. [Fabric] * The fabric file format must be *zfab. * You must enter the weight and thickness of the fabric in the Description. * You must enter information for the applied MAP. (TEXTURE, NORMAL MAP, DISPLACEMENT MAP, OPACITY MAP, ROUGHNESS MAP, METALNESS MAP, BASE MAP) * You must enter the measurement information (whether the equipment is used, the name of the equipment, and the measurement institution) in the Description. * You must enter the fiber content of the fabric in Tag. (e.g., Cotton 100%, Cotton 97%, Spandex 3%) * You must create a file by used for the fabric material according to the repeated image. * The size of the Maps used for fabric material must be 4K or less. [Trim] * The trim file format must be *trm. * The position and rotation of the mesh should be set as 0, and the size should be set to 1. * When making an OBJ trim, the unit of the production environment should be set to mm. * All mesh must be created in Y-axis (up) based environment. * The mesh’s normal direction must be facing outwards. * TRIM must be located at the origin (0,0,0). * Mesh and Texture must match. * In the Description, the following information of the product must be provided. (1) DEFAULT SIZE (X, Y, Z; unit: mm) and WEIGHT (unit: g) of TRIM. (Refer to Property Editor in CLO) (2) UV MAP unwrapping status [Button] * The button file format must be *btn. * The position and rotation of the mesh should be set as 0, and the size should be set to 1. * All mesh must be created in Y-axis (up) based environment. * The mesh’s normal direction should be facing outwards. * The point where the OBJ button will be anchored to the garment must be placed at the origin (0,0,0)). * When making an OBJ button, the unit of the production environment should be set to mm. * The top side of the button should be made in the positive Y-axis direction. * Mesh and texture must be matched. * In the Description, the following information of the product must be provided. (1) DEFAULT SIZE (X, Y, Z; unit: mm) and WEIGHT (unit: g) of BUTTON. (Refer to Property Editor in CLO) (2) UV MAP unwrapping status * If you make a Thread button, Additional Cross THREAD TYPE is required. * If you make a Thread button, Mesh needs to be renamed as REN_BUTTON, REN_THREAD. [Buttonhole] * The buttonhole file format must be *bth. * The image of the buttonhole must have a transparent background and be saved in PNG format. * Buttonhole Images must be black and white with no color value. * Buttonhole Image should not show aliasing. * Buttonhole Image must be registered as horizontal orientation. (Please refer to the example image below.)![buttonhole.png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775615709849) * In the Description, the following information of the product must be provided. (1) DEFAULT SIZE of the buttonhole. You can also write in button units or provide information in Width & Length & Thickness values. [Zipper Puller] * The puller(zipper) file format must be *zpl or *zpu. * When registering the zipper file, it will be all created in size #3. Please create the slider file(OBJ) in size #3. (#3 refers to the zipper size of approximately 3 mm wide zipper teeth when closed.) * The mesh’s normal direction must be facing outwards. * Place the puller on the slider to the origin (0,0,0). *Puller Position can be adjusted within CLO software. * In the Description, the following information of the product must be provided. (1) Vertex Counts (2) UV MAP unwrapping status [Zipper Slider] * The slider(zipper) file format must be *zsd or *zsl. * Slider should be created as OBJ file format. * When registering the zipper file, it will be all created in size #3. Please create the slider file(OBJ) in size #3. (#3 refers to the zipper size of approximately 3 mm wide zipper teeth when closed.) * The mesh’s normal direction must be facing outwards. * Align the MESH position according to the purpose of each axis. (If the position of the axis is not aligned, OBJ might not be created in the right place when creating a zipper.) X-axis | Place the point where the zipper tape touches the slider on the X-axis of 0. ---|--- Y-axis | Slider’s moving direction is on Y-axis. The point where the zipper closes and where it touches should be placed on the Y-axis of 0. Z-axis | Place the face of the zipper tape of a slider on the Z-axis of 0. * In the Description, the following information of the product must be provided. (1) Vertex Counts (2) UV MAP unwrapping status [Zipper Slider&Puller] * The slider & puller(zipper) file format must be *zss. * Slider&Puller should be created as OBJ file format. * When registering the zipper file, it will be all created in size #3. Please create the slider file(OBJ) in size #3. (#3 refers to the zipper size of approximately 3 mm wide zipper teeth when closed.) * The mesh’s normal direction must be facing outwards. * Align the MESH position according to the purpose of each axis. (_Same as the axis of the Slider)_ X-axis | Place the point where the zipper tape touches each stopper on the X-axis of 0. ---|--- Y-axis | Slider’s moving direction is on Y-axis. The point where the zipper closes and where it touches should be placed on the Y-axis of 0. Z-axis | Place the face of the zipper teeth of a slider on the Z-axis of 0. * In the Description, the following information of the product must be provided. (1) Vertex Counts (2) UV MAP unwrapping status [Zipper Top Stopper] * The stopper(zipper) file format must be *zsp or *zsl. * Stopper should be created as OBJ file format. * When registering the zipper file, it will be all created in size #3. Please create the stopper file(OBJ) in size #3. (#3 refers to the zipper size of approximately 3 mm wide zipper teeth when closed.) * The mesh’s normal direction must be facing outwards. * Create two separate OBJ files for top stoppers, as shown below. ![topstopper.png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775647956505) * Align the MESH position according to the purpose of each axis. X-axis | Place the point where the zipper tape touches each stopper on the X-axis of 0. ---|--- Y-axis | The top of the zipper tape and where they touch should be placed on the Y-axis of 0. Z-axis | Place the face of the zipper teeth of a slider on the Z-axis of 0. * In the Description, the following information of the product must be provided. (1) Vertex Counts (2) UV MAP unwrapping status [Zipper Bottom Stopper] * The stopper(zipper) file format must be *zsp or *zsl. * Stopper should be created as OBJ file format. * When registering the zipper file, it will be all created in size #3. Please create the stopper file(OBJ) in size #3. (#3 refers to the zipper size of approximately 3 mm wide zipper teeth when closed.) * The mesh’s normal direction must be facing outwards. * Create two separate OBJ files for bottom stoppers, as shown below. ![bottomstopper.png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775656854041) * The Bottom Closed Stopper must be created in one OBJ file ![objfile.png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775657041689) * Align the MESH position according to the purpose of each axis. X-axis | Place the point where the zipper tape touches each stopper on the X-axis of 0. ---|--- Y-axis | When the slider is pulled all the way down, the point where it touches the bottom of the slider should be placed on the Y-axis of 0. Z-axis | Place the face of the zipper teeth of a slider on the Z-axis of 0. * In the Description, the following information of the product must be provided. (1) Vertex Counts (2) UV MAP unwrapping status [Avatar] * The avatar file format must be *avt. * All meshes are created in a Y(up) environment. * Avatar with Joint uses the FBX or OPENCOLLADA format. * Normal direction of the mesh mush face outward. [Hair] * The accessory file must be created in FBX format in order to be registered in the ZACS file. * The normal direction of the mesh must be outward. * The name of the Hair Mesh must be "Hair," case-insensitive. * The Hair FBX should not include anything other than “Hair.” (e.g only select and export Hair Mesh when exporting.) * If you import the Hair FBX with 'Auto Scale' unit, the position and scale of the Hair Mesh must match the avatar you intend to register. * You must specify the name of the avatar that is used to create the accessory file in the description. [Shoes] * The accessory file must be created in FBX format in order to be registered in the ZACS file. * The normal direction of the mesh must face outwards. * The name of the Shoes Mesh must be "Shoes_L" or "Shoes_R," case-insensitive. * The Shoes FBX should not include anything other than “Shoes_L” and “Shoes_R.” (e.g only select and export Shoes Mesh when exporting.) * If you import the Shoes FBX with 'Auto Scale' unit, the position and scale of the Shoes Mesh must match the avatar you intend to register. * For shoes with heels, the heel should have a material separated and applied last. * The name of avatar must be specified in the description so that the customers can recognize which avatar the accessory was made for. [Glasses] * The accessory file must be created in FBX format in order to be registered in the ZACS file. * The normal direction of the mesh must be outward. * The name of the Glasses Mesh must be "Glasses," case-insensitive. * The Glasses FBX should not include anything other than “Glasses.” (e.g only select and export Glasses Mesh when exporting.) * If you import the Glasses FBX with 'Auto Scale' unit, the position and scale of the Glasses Mesh must match the avatar you intend to register. * Due to Glasses ZACS being relatively positioned in the center of the Avatar's nose, the position of Glasses after ZACS transformation may differ from the position of FBX glasses depending on the avatar. * You must specify the name of the avatar that is used to create the accessory file in the description. [Earring] * The accessory file must be created in FBX format in order to be registered in the ZACS file. * The normal direction of the mesh must be outward. * The name of the Earring Mesh must be "Earring," case-insensitive. * The Earring FBX should not include anything other than “Earring.” (e.g only select and export Earring Mesh when exporting.) * If you import the Earring FBX with 'Auto Scale' unit, the position and scale of the Earring Mesh must match the avatar you intend to register. * You must specify the name of the avatar that is used to create the accessory file in the description.

title: Uploading Items
content: ### **Objective** Upload your items on CONNECT. ## **Upload Setting** ### 1\. UPLOAD ITEM Click the **'UPLOAD'** button in the top-right corner of CONNECT. **![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775484370073)** #### ### 2\. Select the type of item to upload * STORE * GALLERY **※ Note:** The size of the upload item must be **less than 500 MB**. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775510238745) ### 3\. CONNECT UPLOAD - Entering Asset Description 1 **When uploading the items to CONNECT, please provide detailed information about the asset for the convenience of customers.** **If detailed information is missing, asset registration may be rejected during the item approval process.** ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775525101849) **① UPLOAD (Mandatory)** Confirm the uploaded asset name and format and replace the file by pressing the **REUPLOAD** button if necessary. **② TITLE (Mandatory)** Please enter the asset name that will be displayed on CONNECT. By default, the uploaded asset's name will be set automatically as the DEFAULT TITLE. **③ DESCRIPTION** DESCRIPTION is allowed up to **2000 characters**. Please check the required information for each item below. ITEM/FORMAT | Must | DESCRIPTION | Example of the DESCRIPTION ---|---|---|--- **Button** **(.BTN)** | | \- X(mm), Y(mm), Z(mm), Weight(g) \- Vertex Counts \- UV MAP unwrapping Status \- If you are selling a physical product, please provide the sales page URL. | (1) Default Size : \- X: 10mm \- Y: 10mm \- Z: 10mm \- Weight: 10g (2) Vertex Counts: 12345 (3) UV MAP Unwrapping Status: O or X AVATAR's Detailed Information \- AVATAR HEIGHT (Scale Unit) \- BUST CIRCUMFERENCE(Scale Unit) \- WAIST CIRCUMFERENCE(Scale Unit) \- HIP CIRCUMFERENCE(Scale Unit) \- Presence of the JOINTS \- \- UV Unwrapping: O or X \- Symmetry: O or X \- Magic Suit : O or X **Scene & Prop** **(.ZSE)** | **Must** | **[Scene]** \- Presence of Light Setting \- UV MAP Unwrapping Status | **[Scene]** (1) Available on FV2 avatars **④ TAGS** **'TAGS'** is a target keyword that helps customers search and amplify your content's reach. Entering the type of assets for sale will help customers when searching for the items. **⑤ ATTACHMENT** You may upload additional files by clicking the **'CHOOSE FILE'** button, and also able to select multiple files. However, it is impossible to track attachment files attached to **'ATTACHMENT'** are being used. Uploading multiple files as a compressed archive is not allowed. Each item must contain only a single file. (They cannot be downloaded from the CONNECT library, and buyers will not be able to view them in the viewer.) **※ Note:** The size of the upload item must be **less than 500 MB**. **⑥ ADD SUB-IMAGES** You can additionally attach the SUB-IMAGES to highlight the item. Upload the files you would like to provide additionally by clicking the **'CHOOSE FILE'** button. **Supported image formats: *.jpg / *.jpeg / *.png** **⑦ THUMBNAIL** You may set or change the Thumbnail. Drag & Drop the thumbnail image into the **'THUMBNAIL BOX'** or click the **'CHOOSE FILE'** button to upload the image. Supported image formats: *.jpg / *.jpeg / *.png Recommended Thumbnail Size: 600 x 800(px) & ratio 3:4 **※ Note:** For the best search result, it is recommended to use English in the title, description, and tags of the item. ## ### 3\. CONNECT UPLOAD - Entering Asset Description 2 ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775551984793) **① SET ITEM CATEGORIES** Detailed categories are provided based on the uploaded item's format, and you can select the specific category for their items in this section. Adding categories will significantly improve the item compatibility and search results. Users can search and filter items by category. **② SET COLLECTION** Users can decide the Collection to include their items. By default, items are assigned to the default collection. Customers can see the items in the assigned collection in their portfolio. **③ PRICING & LICENSE OPTIONS** Users can set the price and license options for their items: **Paid Item** : Select the **'Paid Item'** if you wish to sell the items. **※ Note:** CONNECT charges a **30%** commission on the item's sales. **Free Item** : Select **'Free Item'** to allow users to download their item for free. **※ Note:****Sellers cannot change a 'Free item' to a 'Paid item' after Publication.** **④ BASIC &EXTENDED LICENSE PRICE** Basic License Price: Enable to set the price for the basic license of the item. Extended License Price: Enable to set the price of the extended license 1 to 8 times the item's price. **⑤ PHYSICAL PRODUCTION** Sellers can allow physical production by clicking the **'Physical Production'** checkbox. ※ The following option will be limited if the original item is not allowed for physical production. **⑥ PUBLISH OPTIONS** Click the **'PUBLISH'** button to publish the item: **'PAID ITEM'** goes through review before publishing. It stays in **'DRAFT'** status until the review team approves. During the **'DRAFT'** status, creators can edit or re-upload the item. **'FREE ITEM'** will be published without any approval. Clicking the **'DRAFT'** button makes the item invisible to other users and allows you to either edit or re-upload. **⑦ BACK / UPLOAD** Click the **'BACK'** button to return to the previous step or the **'UPLOAD'** button to proceed to the next step. ### 4\. PREVIEW PAGE You can check whether the uploaded files and item information are correctly registered before publishing. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775542395033) **① ITEM STATUS** You can check the current status of the item. **'PAID ITEM'** will stay in **'DRAFT,'** hidden from other users, until the review team approves it. Upon approval, the status of the 'PAID ITEM' will change to 'PUBLISH.' **'FREE ITEM'** will be published without any approval. **② DELETE / EDIT** You can delete the uploaded files or item information by clicking the **'DELETE'** button. You can change the uploaded files or item information by clicking the **'EDIT'** button.
content_description: The purpose of this webpage is to guide users through the process of uploading items to CONNECT, ensuring they provide all necessary details for successful asset registration and approval.

title: Thumbnail Guide
content: **Guide** Recommend creating thumbnail images based on the following criteria below. **Details** * Recommend![thumbnail](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775603046297) * High-Resolution images * Recommended image size: 900*1200 * Image ratio: 3:4 (portrait) * Supported image formats: .jpeg /.png /.bmp * Supported video format for motion(.mtn): .webp * Videos in formats other than WEBP (e.g. MP4, AVI, etc.) must be converted to WEBP and uploaded as a thumbnail. * Clear visibility of items in the image. * High-Quality Images and items. * Avoid including multiple images in one thumbnail. * Recommend using a simple/solid background, so that item stands out. * Rejected * When only a part of the item is shown in the thumbnail. (paid item) * Ex) In the thumbnail, it appears as a single item, but the item file is a set. * When items other than the ones being sold are included in the thumbnail. (paid item) * Ex) Thumbnail contains 3 pieces (top + bottom + vest), but only 2 pieces (top + bottom) have been uploaded. * Differences in details between the thumbnail and item. (paid item) * Ex) The item in the file does not have a pocket, while the item shown in the thumbnail does have a pocket. * Differences between the default colors of the thumbnail and item. (paid item) * The item's color in the thumbnail must match the color of the item shown in CLO's 3D viewer when the file is opened. * The first colorway from the list will appear in CONNECT's 3D viewer, which is different from CLO's 3D Viewer. * Differences between the colors of the thumbnail and item. (paid item) * Differences in materials between the thumbnail and the item being sold. (free, paid item) * The item being sold differs from the item in the thumbnail. * The item in the thumbnail is not clearly visible. * Inappropriate Thumbnail * Using real-life photos * Uploading screenshots of software instead of rendered images * Uploading unrelated images for the item. * Uploading provocative images * In the naked image, without wearing underwear or being covered by any object (a mannequin, solid color avatar does not apply to this) * Copyright Infringement (free, paid item) * Using Brand names or Logos. * Using names or images of specific individuals or characters. * Duplicate Thumbnails * Uploading the same duplicated images with only slight design modifications * Uploading the same thumbnail multiple times
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for creating effective thumbnail images that adhere to specific quality, format, and content criteria to enhance visibility and compliance.

title: Data retention period
content: ## ## CLO‘s Utilization of CONNECT items ● Items uploaded on CONNECT can be used by CLO and its global affiliates for advertising, exhibitions, marketing, and other purposes. ● Items uploaded on CONNECT can be utilized by CLO and its global affiliates for research and collaboration purposes. ## Item deletion ● Even if a seller deletes an item, the buyer can still download the purchased item for up to 2 years. ## Service withdrawal ● In the event of a seller withdrawing from the service, buyers can still download purchased items for up to 2 years.
content_description: This web page outlines the utilization of CONNECT items by CLO and its global affiliates, detailing their use for marketing and research, as well as policies on item deletion and service withdrawal.

title: Blocking items
content: ## When Items are Blocked ● Items, either in whole or in part, may be blocked if they infringe on someone else's copyright. ● Items that are explicit or violent may be blocked. ● Items containing messages that are potentially controversial in areas such as politics or religion may be blocked. ● Items that cause discomfort to other users or receive continuous reports may be blocked. ● In cases where items are deemed incompatible with the policies of CONNECT, administrators may block them. ## Revenue when Paid Items are Blocked ● If a paid item is blocked, sales will be discontinued. ● Revenue from already sold items will be paid to the seller. ● If the reason for blocking the item is related to copyright, ownership of revenue from already sold items may be determined through legal procedures or discussions with the original creator. ● If a blocked item is used as a Design Source, generating revenue, the seller will not receive any revenue.
content_description: This webpage outlines the policies and procedures regarding the blocking of items that violate copyright, contain explicit content, or are deemed controversial, along with the implications for revenue related to paid items that are blocked.

title: Payout method
content: ## Payment through PayPal ● Revenue will be paid through the PayPal account you entered when filling out the Seller Info. Additional Guidance * If there are issues with your PayPal account, payments will be temporarily suspended, and you will receive a request to resubmit Seller Info. * If you wish to change the PayPal account receiving the revenue, you must resubmit Seller Info. If the newly submitted Seller Info is not approved before the payment date, the payment may be deferred to the next month. ## Payment through Bank Transfer ● For sellers who cannot use PayPal, payment through wire transfer will be processed twice a year. ● Payments are made in June and December. How to Receive Payment via Wire Transfer 1\. Provide the following information to the administrator through the [Connect inquiry:](https://connect-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/requests/new) * CONNECT Name * CONNECT (CLO-SET) account * Name (real name) * Swift code * IBAN (International Bank Account Number) * Country (with bank account) 2\. Submit Seller Info. * When submitting Seller Info, enter the PayPal account as follows: (ex- [withoutpaypal@clo-set.com )](mailto:withoutpaypal@clo-set.com) Additional Guidance * Payment through bank transfer is only possible for countries that cannot use PayPal or under special circumstances. * Even if you have provided bank account information, if Seller Info is submitted and fails the inspection, earnings will not be paid. * If both steps 1 and 2 are completed, earnings will be transferred to the registered account in June and December. You may receive an email confirming the completion of PayPal payment, but it has been transferred to the bank account, so you may disregard it. * If you want to change the bank account information, you must resend the information for step 1 before the payment is delivered.
content_description: This webpage provides essential information on receiving payments via PayPal and bank transfer, including procedures for submitting Seller Info and guidelines for account changes.

title: Payout Schedule
content: ## Payout in the following month ● Revenue from items sold between the 1st and last day of each month will be settled in the following month. ● Payout dates fall between the 15th and 30th of the following month, subject to variation due to holidays or maintenance. ## Wire Transfer Schedule ● Revenue from December to May will be paid out in June. ● Revenue from June to November will be paid in December. ● If an account has an issue on the payout day, it will be postponed to the next scheduled payout day. ## Refund Policy ● Refunds due to technical issues or payment cancellations will be deducted from the final revenue before the settlement date.
content_description: This webpage provides essential information regarding payout schedules, wire transfer timelines, and refund policies for revenue generated from item sales.

title: Payout conditions
content: To process settlement, ensure the following conditions are met: ## Seller's Information Verification ● Once seller's information is verified, the payout will be processed. ● Revenue accumulates before verification; the payout is available once seller info is verified. ● When seller information is changed after initial verification, payout will be delayed for re-verification. ## Payout Available over USD $50 ● Access payout when total revenue, after fee deduction, exceeds USD $50. ● If revenue is under USD $50, expected payout accumulates. ● The payout is based on the sales revenue of $50 USD (taxes are not included). If you have US-resident buyers, their tax is deducted from the final payout. Note that the actual payout may vary after tax deductions. ## Payout Delayed ● Payout delays occur in the presence of copyright issues until resolution. ● Majority of buyer refund requests or submitted reports result in payout delay until it is solved. ● Payout will be temporarily disabled in cases of suspicious payments or payment system issues.
content_description: This webpage outlines the conditions and processes for seller payout settlements, including verification requirements, minimum payout thresholds, and potential delays due to various factors.

title: Design Source Policy
content: ## ## Create items using paid items (garments/trims/fabrics) ● You may sell created items by using paid items(garments/ trims/ fabrics). ● Garments can be purchased, modified, and sold as a second creation on CONNECT. ● However, trims and fabrics cannot be modified and re-sell. Trims can be only included in garments. ## Settlement when using paid items ● When created garments consist of paid items as a Design Source, the price of paid items will be added to your set price. ● When garments consisting of paid items are sold, the revenue of the Design Source will be distributed to the original creator. ## Revenue when your items are sold as Design Source ● When your items are sold and used as Design Source for other items, your items will be settled as your revenue. ## Examples ● Seller D created garments by purchasing Seller A's garment($10), Seller B's trim($2), Seller C's fabric($5). ● When Seller D sets the price of the garment, the total price will be automatically set as the sum of items A, B, and C, which is $17. ● When Seller D sets the margin as $20, the total price will be $37. ● When items are sold at $37, Seller D's revenue will be $20, Seller A's will be $10, Seller B's $2, Seller C's $5. ![10.png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775672976153)
content_description: This webpage outlines the guidelines for creating and selling garments using paid items, detailing how revenue is distributed among creators based on their contributions.

title: Deduction amount & Payout amount
content: The calculation of the seller's earnings is as follows. **Total item sales amount** **(-) Design Source usage fee** **(-) Website deduction commission** **(-) Withholding tax** ## ## **Total item sales amount** ● Total amount of items sold from the first to the last day of the month ● Includes items sold through Design Source when other sellers' items are sold (When someone resells my item as a component in a garment file, the price of my item is included in my sales revenue) ## (-) **Design Source usage fee** ● If paid items are used, the revenue is shared with the seller who created those items. (When a paid garment, fabric, or trims are purchased to create a paid garment, and the garment is sold, the price of the included paid items is categorized as the sales revenue of the seller of those items) ## (-) **Website Commission Deduction** ● 70% of the total sales amount is allocated as the seller's revenue, while 30% is deducted as a service fee. ## (-) **Withholding tax** ● For orders where the buyer is American, a withholding tax may be additionally applied. ● The withholding tax rate is calculated based on the agreed upon rate between the United States and the seller's country. ## [Example] ● Without using Design Source, a $100 item was created and sold, with the buyer not being from the United States, * Total Sales Amount: $100 (-) Website Commission: $30 = **Total Payment: $70** ● Using $10 fabric, a $100 item was created and sold, with the buyer not being from the United States, * Total Sales Amount: $100 (-) Cost of Design Source Fabric: $10 (-) Website Commission: $27(30%) = **Total Payment:****$63** ● A Polish individual created a $100 item without using Design Source and sold it to a buyer from the United States, * Total Sales Amount: $100 (-) Website Commission(30%): $30 = User's Earnings: $70 (-) Withholding Tax (5% between Poland and the United States): $3.5 =**Total Payment: $66.5** ● A Korean individual created a $100 item using $30 buttons and sold it to a buyer from the United States, * Total Sales Amount: $100 (-) Cost of Design Source Buttons: $30 (-) Website Commission(30%): $21 = User's Earnings: $49 (-) Withholding Tax (10% between South Korea and the United States): $4.9 = **Total Payment:****$44.1**
content_description: This web page provides a clear breakdown of how seller earnings are calculated, including deductions for Design Source usage fees, website commissions, and withholding taxes, to help sellers understand their net revenue from item sales.
